howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: A simple, personalised process — expert guidance, clear pricing, and support from start to finish.

step1.title: Tell us about your situation
step1.tagline: Start with a form or email.
step1.description: Tell us about your situation, what you want to achieve, and how we can help. Our team will review your case and determine the best way to assist you.

step2.title: We assess your case
step2.tagline: Personalised advice, when you need it.
step2.description: Once we review your situation, we'll come back to you with an initial assessment and the next steps.

step3.title: Receive your personalised proposal
step3.tagline: Clear pricing based on your case.
step3.description: Every immigration case is different. Once we understand how we can help, we'll provide you with an estimated price and a clear overview of the services included.

step4.title: We handle the process
step4.tagline: You stay informed. We take care of the rest.
step4.description: From completing forms correctly to preparing applications and communicating with your local Town Hall and relevant authorities, we handle the process with you and keep you informed every step of the way.

meta.title: Sworn translations in Belgium | Avilo
meta.description: Sworn translations of civil records, court judgments and notarial deeds for Belgian authorities, by a sworn translator registered in Belgium.

hero.title: Sworn translations for Belgian authorities
hero.sub: Civil records, court judgments and notarial deeds, translated by a sworn translator registered in Belgium.

translator.title: Your translator
translator.body1: Our sworn translator, Elouise Verheyen, is based in Ghent and registered in the Belgian National Register of Sworn Translators under number {vti}.
translator.body2: Her Dutch translations use Belgian legal terminology, not terminology from the Netherlands. This matters when a document is filed with a Belgian commune, court or the Immigration Office.
translator.registerLink: Check her registration in the official register

documents.title: Documents we translate

civilStatus.title: Civil status
civilStatus.items: Birth, marriage and divorce certificates, Spanish Libro de Familia, population register extracts, nationality and residence certificates

administrativeDecision.title: Administrative decisions
administrativeDecision.items: For example, German social benefit decisions

documents.uses: Common uses are family reunification, residence permits, nationality applications, marriage registration and recognition of foreign judgments.

sworn.title: What makes it a sworn translation
sworn.fidelity: Full fidelity: nothing is added, left out or corrected. Stamps, seals, signatures and QR codes are described in brackets where they appear.
sworn.certification: Every page carries "Voor eensluidende vertaling". The last page has the certification clause, signature and VTI number.
sworn.delivery: Delivered as a PDF with a qualified electronic signature, plus a hand-signed copy.
sworn.legalization: Legalization through FPS Foreign Affairs (eLegalization) is available if the receiving authority asks for it.

steps.title: How it works
steps.step1: Send a scan of your document.
steps.step2: Receive a quote within two business days.
steps.step4: The translation is prepared and certified.
steps.step5: Receive the signed PDF and pay the balance. Legalization is optional.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.minimum: Minimum €90 for standard documents, €115 for complex ones (VAT included).
pricing.factors: The final price depends on word count, layout, number of stamps, scan quality and terminology. You get an exact quote after we see the document.
pricing.turnaround: 2–3 business days for short documents. Longer projects are scheduled with you.

original.q: Do I need to send the original?
original.a: A clear scan or photo is enough to quote and translate. If the authority needs the hand-signed copy, we post or hand it over.

acceptance.q: Will the authority accept the translation?
acceptance.a: Translations by a sworn translator registered in Belgium are accepted by Belgian authorities. Some ask for legalization as well. Check with the receiving office, or ask us.

apostille.q: Do I also need an apostille or legalization of the original document?
apostille.a: That depends on the country that issued it and on the authority receiving it. It is separate from the translation. We can tell you what usually applies.

payment.a: 50% when you accept the quote, 50% on delivery.

privacy.a: Your files are used only for your translation and are deleted six months after delivery.

otherPairs.q: Can you translate other language pairs?
otherPairs.a: Not at the moment. The pairs above are the ones we certify.
